items.title: Team Leadership & Development Standards
items.description: Leading an 11-person cross-functional team meant turning delivery quality from individual capability into process: architecture decisions settled before work begins, implementation quality held by code review, release risk controlled by a checklist, troubleshooting steps documented. Explicit rules and acceptance criteria are also what later made adopting AI possible.

items.title: AI Applications & AI-Assisted Development
items.description: AI is both tooling and product. On the development side, standards are written as agent-readable rule files with automated verification loops so the agent judges its own compliance, shortening the iteration cycle. On the product side, six Claude features shipped with two behind subscription tiers, handling guardrails, degradation, content moderation, and cost accounting. At Pacificsmart I extended this into a team workflow: an Asana card dispatches work to an agent automatically, and MRs are AI-reviewed and merged by risk tier.

items.title: Hands-on Engineering & Architecture Judgment
items.description: I still build hands-on and can take schema, APIs, frontend, and deployment end to end on my own; Bound was mine from product strategy and UI design through full-stack implementation. Architecture decisions rest on actual query shapes and cost, such as indexes designed around real queries and caching split between in-process memory and Redis. As a tech lead, this keeps technical decisions grounded in executable detail.
